 By Donna Lind PUBLISHED: November 7, 2026 at 12:45 PM PST | UPDATED: November 7, 2026 at 2:01 PM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... As we approach the winter season, emergency preparedness is an important priority for the city of Scotts Valley. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration is forecasting a strong El Niño this winter, which can increase the potential for significant storms and rainfall in California. While the impacts on Santa Cruz County remain uncertain, we know from past experience how quickly heavy rain, flooding, fallen trees and power outages can affect our community.
 The city of Scotts Valley has been taking proactive steps to prepare. City staff participated in emergency preparedness training to strengthen coordination and response capabilities. Additional storm-response equipment has been placed in Scotts Valley Police Department vehicles, allowing officers to assist during emergencies while public works crews respond. Our public works and wastewater teams have also been preparing critical infrastructure for the rainy season.
 The city continues to coordinate with Santa Cruz County and local public safety partners on emergency planning and response. Residents should sign up for CruzAware emergency alerts and learn their evacuation zone before a storm occurs. Visit CruzAware.org for alert registration and county emergency information.
 Public works
 • Clearing and inspecting storm drains, culverts and drainage channels, prioritizing known flooding and problem areas.
 • Inspecting previous storm-damage sites along Bean Creek Road and Glenwood Drive, as well as other vulnerable slopes and retaining walls.
 • Reviewing active construction sites for drainage, erosion controls and unfinished work that may be affected by wet weather.
 • Addressing selected high-risk trees to reduce the potential for falling trees, property damage and blocked roads.
 • Ensuring sand, sandbags and other storm-response supplies are ready for the rainy season.
 • Preparing road-closure equipment and reviewing alternate access routes for vulnerable locations.
 • Coordinating with public safety partners and monitoring forecasts to prepare crews and resources ahead of storms.
 Wastewater Division
 The Wastewater Division has also been preparing for the impacts of heavy rainfall. Additional equipment has been installed to remotely monitor sewer conditions and provide early warning of potential issues. Staff continue preventive maintenance at sewer lift stations to keep pumps and equipment ready for wet weather. These measures support a quicker response when problems arise.
 Create an emergency plan
 Prepare a plan with everyone in your household:
 • Identify two ways to leave your home and know your evacuation zone and alternate routes.
 • Determine a place where family members can reunite if separated during an evacuation.
 • Include pets and anyone who may need additional assistance.
 • Practice your plan and review it periodically with everyone in your household.
 Evaluate your home ahead of time:
 • Know when and how to turn off electricity and gas, if directed by emergency officials or utilities.
 • Locate fire extinguishers, check smoke alarms and learn to open your garage door manually.
 • Check gutters and drainage areas, secure outdoor items and prepare for possible power outages.
 Build an emergency supply kit
 Food and water:
 • Store at least one gallon of water per person per day and nonperishable food that can be prepared without power.
 • Include a non-electric can opener and any needed baby or pet food.
 Equipment:
 • Keep flashlights, extra batteries, a battery-powered or hand-crank radio, and portable phone chargers available.
 Emergency go-kit:
 • Include prescription medications, first aid supplies, copies of important documents, cash and hygiene supplies.
 • Add supplies for babies, older adults, people with disabilities and pets as needed.
 For additional guidance on emergency alerts, evacuation zones, household planning and supplies, visit the city’s Emergency Preparedness webpage at scottsvalley.gov/826/Emergency-Preparedness .
 Thank you to the city employees in public works, wastewater, police and other departments who prepare for emergencies and respond when our community needs them. Taking these steps together will help Scotts Valley be ready for whatever this winter brings.
 Donna Lind is the mayor of Scotts Valley.
